title: Miso-Glazed Cod
subtitle: Japanese-style cod with a white miso and mirin glaze
excerpt: Cod fillets marinated in a simple white miso and mirin glaze then roasted at high heat until lacquered and caramelised at the edges. The marinade takes five minutes to mix and the fish needs 30 minutes to soak up the flavour before it goes into the oven.
sourceNotes: Based on the Japanese miso-marinated fish technique, most famously associated with Nobu Matsuhisa's black cod.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate for up to 24 hours in the fridge for deeper flavour.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 200C / Gas 7. Or finish under a hot grill for 3 minutes.

content.text: The marinade will caramelise fast at high heat. Line the baking tray with foil to avoid it burning onto the pan, and watch the fish from the 8-minute mark. If it colours before it is cooked through, tent loosely with foil for the last few minutes.

items.prepNote: 4 fillets, about 150g each, skin on or off

content.text: Mix together the white miso, mirin, sake, honey, and sesame oil in a shallow dish.
Add the cod fillets and turn to coat on both sides. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 24 hours.
Preheat the oven to 220C. Line a baking tray with foil.
Lift the cod fillets from the marinade and place on the lined tray. Wipe off any very thick coating so it does not burn.
Roast for 10 to 12 minutes until the fish is just cooked through and the glaze is caramelised and slightly charred at the edges.
Scatter with sliced spring onion and serve with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Glaze has burned before fish is cooked
items.cause: Oven too hot or glaze too thick
items.fix: Tent with foil and lower heat to 180C for 5 minutes more.

items.symptom: Fish is sticking to the tray
items.cause: Foil not used or glaze burned on
items.fix: Always line the tray with foil for this recipe.
